::: {#def-bma}
#### Bayesian model averaging

Let $M_1, \ldots, M_K$ be candidate models
with prior probabilities $\p(M_k)$ summing to 1,
and let $\p(\vy \mid M_k)$ be the [marginal likelihood](bayesian-inference.qmd#def-marginal-likelihood)
of the data under model $M_k$.
The **posterior model probabilities** are

$$
\p(M_k \mid \vy) \eqdef
\frac{\p(\vy \mid M_k)\, \p(M_k)}{\sum_{l=1}^K \p(\vy \mid M_l)\, \p(M_l)},
$$

and **Bayesian model averaging** estimates a quantity $\Delta$
that has the same meaning in every model
by its posterior distribution averaged over the models:

$$
\p(\Delta \mid \vy) \eqdef \sum_{k=1}^K \p(\Delta \mid M_k, \vy)\, \p(M_k \mid \vy).
$$
:::
